studies.Authors: Cho E, Holmes MD, Hankinson SE, Willett WC
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Nutrient intake was assessed using a validated food-frequency questionnaire six times since 1984.

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Participants in the highest quintile of intakes had multivariate relative risks of 1.10 (95% confidence interval (95% CI): 0.99-1.22; P-value, test for trend=0.14) for choline
extraction_supporting_text.effect_direction: choline ... intake was not associated with a reduced risk of post-menopausal breast cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.outcome_definition: 3990 incident cases of invasive breast cancer.

headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger's test indicates no significant funnel plot asymmetry (p=0.1086). The distribution of studies appears symmetric, suggesting a lower risk of publication bias.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 4 studies yielded an effect size of 0.76 (95% CI: 0.52–1.11), indicating no statistically significant association between choline and breast cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 90.52%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
